title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 7
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Visitors last season and the number of guided walks run at five nature reserves:

Ambleside: 6,400 visitors, 18 walks
Brackley: 9,800 visitors, 35 walks
Colwyn: 4,100 visitors, 9 walks
Dartmoor: 12,600 visitors, 48 walks
Ennerdale: 7,300 visitors, 22 walks

Which reserve had the most visitors for each walk it ran?
options: A. Ambleside
B. Brackley
C. Colwyn
D. Dartmoor
E. Ennerdale
questions.explanation: Visitors divided by walks: Ambleside 356, Brackley 280, Colwyn 456, Dartmoor 263, Ennerdale 332. Colwyn is highest. The busiest reserve overall also runs the most walks, so it is not the one drawing most people per walk.

questions.prompt:
Monthly enquiries received by an agency:

Mar: 214
Apr: 268
May: 262
Jun: 331

In which month was the percentage rise over the previous month greatest?
options: A. June
B. April
C. May
D. The rise was equal each month
E. Enquiries fell in every month
questions.explanation: Month on month: Apr +25.2%, May -2.2%, Jun +26.3%. Jun is largest at 26.3%. June adds more enquiries in absolute terms but rises from a larger base.

questions.prompt:
A haulier's costs by category:

Fuel: 39%
Wages: 27%
Maintenance: 15%
Insurance: 11%
Depot: 5%
Other: 3%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for at least 80% of costs?
options: A. Two
B. Five
C. Six
D. Three
E. Four
questions.explanation: Largest first: 39 + 27 = 66%, short of 80. Adding Maintenance reaches 81%. So 3 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Two groups sat the same assessment:

Group A: 30 candidates, mean score 68
Group B: 90 candidates, mean score 52

What is the mean score across all candidates?
questions.explanation: Weight by candidate numbers: (30 × 68 + 90 × 52) / 120 = 56.0. The unweighted average of the two means is 60.0, too high because the larger group scored lower.

questions.prompt:
Two letting agents charge for managing a property:

Agent One: 14% of the rent collected, no fixed fee
Agent Two: GBP 220.00 a year plus 5% of the rent collected

Select the annual rent at which the two cost the same AND the cheaper agent on rent of GBP 3,000.00 a year.
options: A. GBP 2,444.00; Agent One is cheaper at GBP 3,000.00
B. GBP 1,500.00; Agent One is cheaper at GBP 3,000.00
C. GBP 2,444.00; the two cost the same at GBP 3,000.00
D. GBP 4,000.00; Agent Two is cheaper at GBP 3,000.00
E. GBP 2,444.00; Agent Two is cheaper at GBP 3,000.00
questions.explanation: Equal when 0.14r = 220 + 0.05r, so r = 220/0.09 = GBP 2,444.00. At GBP 3,000.00: One charges GBP 420.00, Two charges GBP 370.00, so Agent Two is cheaper below the crossover.

questions.prompt:
Two delivery routes yesterday:

Route A: 170 drops, average value GBP 9.20
Route B: 96 drops, average value GBP 14.80

Select the route with the higher total value delivered AND the route with the higher value per drop.
options: A. Route A on both measures
B. Route B on total; Route A on value per drop
C. Route A on total; Route B on value per drop
D. Route B on both measures
E. The two routes are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Totals: Route A GBP 1,564.00, Route B GBP 1,420.80. Value per drop is given: Route A GBP 9.20, Route B GBP 14.80. Volume and value point to different routes, so one figure alone cannot rank them.

questions.prompt:
A publisher's fixed costs for a title are GBP 18,400.00. Each copy sells for GBP 96.00 and costs GBP 58.00 to produce.

Select the number of copies needed to break even AND the number needed for a profit of GBP 12,000.00.
options: A. 485 to break even; 800 for the target
B. 485 to break even; 970 for the target
C. 300 to break even; 800 for the target
D. 485 to break even; 900 for the target
E. 500 to break even; 1,000 for the target
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 38.00 a copy. Break-even is GBP 18,400.00 / GBP 38.00 = 485 copies. Covering GBP 30,400.00 needs 800 copies.

questions.prompt:
Two systems, each with an installation cost and an annual running cost expressed as a percentage of it:

Scheme P: install GBP 4,800.00, running 9% of install a year
Scheme Q: install GBP 7,100.00, running 4% of install a year

Select the cheaper system over 4 years AND over 12 years, counting installation plus running costs.
options: A. Scheme P at both horizons
B. Scheme Q at both horizons
C. Scheme Q at 4 years; Scheme P at 12 years
D. Scheme P at 4 years; Scheme P at 12 years
E. The two are equal at both horizons
questions.explanation: Over 4 years: Scheme P GBP 6,528.00, Scheme Q GBP 8,236.00. Over 12 years: Scheme P GBP 9,984.00, Scheme Q GBP 10,508.00. The cheaper installation wins over a short horizon and loses over a long one.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): cases handled — Team A 640, Team B 1,520, Team C 980

SOURCE 2 (table): cases escalated — Team A 41, Team B 68, Team C 59

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Coaching should go to the team escalating the highest proportion of its cases."

Which team should receive coaching on that criterion?
options: A. Team A
B. Team B
C. Team C
D. The three teams are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Escalation rates: Team A 6.4%, Team B 4.5%, Team C 6.0%. Team A is highest. Team B escalates the most cases in total but handles far more of them.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our defect rate fell from 2.4% to 1.1% after the new inspection regime."

SOURCE 2 (note): "Under the new regime, defects are counted only when found at final inspection; those caught and reworked earlier on the line are logged as rework."

SOURCE 3 (table): rework events rose from 310 to 1,180 over the same period.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Quality improved by more than half
B. Much of the fall is a change in what counts as a defect rather than in how many occur
C. The new regime caused more defects
D. Rework and defects are the same thing
E. The defect rate cannot be measured under either regime
questions.explanation: The definition narrowed and the excluded category grew almost fourfold, so the headline fall partly reflects reclassification. Option C overstates in the other direction: the sources do not show total faults rising, only that they are now recorded differently.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): workers on site — Site X 3,400, Site Y 11,800, Site Z 7,600

SOURCE 2 (table): reportable incidents per 100 workers — Site X 6.2, Site Y 1.4, Site Z 2.9

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each incident takes the same investigator time, so target the site producing the most incidents."

Which site produces the most incidents?
options: A. Site X
B. Site Y
C. All three produce the same number
D. Site Z
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Incidents are workers multiplied by the rate per hundred: Site X 211, Site Y 165, Site Z 220. Site Z is highest. Site X has much the worst rate but too few workers to lead on the count.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Average class size fell from 27.4 to 24.1 pupils."

SOURCE 2 (table): pupil numbers fell from 1,096 to 940 over the same period, and the number of classes was unchanged at 40.

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The reduction shows our investment in additional teaching capacity."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Teaching capacity rose by about 12%
B. The school added classes to reduce class sizes
C. Class sizes fell because more teachers were recruited
D. The figures in Source 1 are inconsistent with Source 2
E. Class sizes fell because there are fewer pupils, not because capacity was added
questions.explanation: 940 pupils across 40 classes averages 23.5, close to the reported 24.1, and the class count did not change. The fall follows from the smaller intake, so Source 3's claim is not supported — and option D is wrong, since the two sources are broadly consistent.

questions.prompt:
A bookshop sold 120 books, some hardback at GBP 22.00 and the rest paperback at GBP 9.00. How many hardbacks were sold?

(1) Takings were GBP 1,730.00.
(2) Paperbacks outsold hardbacks by 20.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1): 9(120 - h) + 22h = 1,730 gives 1,080 + 13h = 1,730, so h = 50 - sufficient. From (2): p - h = 20 with p + h = 120 also gives h = 50 - sufficient. Each statement alone fixes the number, and the two agree, so the answer is D rather than C.

questions.prompt:
What is the perimeter of a rectangle?

(1) Its area is 48 square metres.
(2) Its length is three times its width.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) alone allows many shapes. (2) alone fixes the proportions but not the size. Together, 3w x w = 48 gives w = 4 and length 12, so the perimeter is 32 m.

questions.prompt:
Is the average of four numbers greater than 50?

(1) Their total is 210.
(2) The largest is 90.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives an average of 52.5, which answers the question definitively - sufficient. (2) says nothing about the other three, which could be tiny or large.

questions.prompt:
How many members voted in favour?

(1) Two thirds of those voting were in favour.
(2) 40 members voted against.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives a proportion with no total; (2) gives a count of the other side. Together, the 40 against are one third of the vote, so 80 voted in favour.

questions.prompt:
Which depot earns the most revenue per vehicle?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 vehicles | Annual revenue | Driver satisfaction
Aylsham | 340 | 2.6 | GBP 512,000.00 | 63
Bickley | 205 | 4.1 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88
Chalfont | 470 | 1.9 | GBP 690,000.00 | 54
Draycott | 160 | 5.3 | GBP 246,000.00 | 84
Elstree | 395 | 3.2 | GBP 578,000.00 | 71
Fordham | 260 | 2.2 | GBP 402,000.00 | 79
options: A. Aylsham
B. Bickley
C. Chalfont
D. Draycott
E. Elstree
questions.explanation: Revenue divided by vehicles: Aylsham GBP 1,505.88, Bickley GBP 1,551.22, Chalfont GBP 1,468.09, Draycott GBP 1,537.50, Elstree GBP 1,463.29, Fordham GBP 1,546.15. Bickley is highest. The depot with the largest revenue also runs the most vehicles.

questions.prompt:
How many depots have a breakdown rate above the mean for the six?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 vehicles | Annual revenue | Driver satisfaction
Aylsham | 340 | 2.6 | GBP 512,000.00 | 63
Bickley | 205 | 4.1 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88
Chalfont | 470 | 1.9 | GBP 690,000.00 | 54
Draycott | 160 | 5.3 | GBP 246,000.00 | 84
Elstree | 395 | 3.2 | GBP 578,000.00 | 71
Fordham | 260 | 2.2 | GBP 402,000.00 | 79
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Two
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: Mean breakdown rate is (2.6 + 4.1 + 1.9 + 5.3 + 3.2 + 2.2) / 6 = 3.22. Above it: Bickley 4.1, Draycott 5.3 — 2 depots.

questions.prompt:
Which depot suffers the greatest number of breakdowns a year?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 vehicles | Annual revenue | Driver satisfaction
Aylsham | 340 | 2.6 | GBP 512,000.00 | 63
Bickley | 205 | 4.1 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88
Chalfont | 470 | 1.9 | GBP 690,000.00 | 54
Draycott | 160 | 5.3 | GBP 246,000.00 | 84
Elstree | 395 | 3.2 | GBP 578,000.00 | 71
Fordham | 260 | 2.2 | GBP 402,000.00 | 79
options: A. Aylsham
B. Bickley
C. Chalfont
D. Fordham
E. Elstree
questions.explanation: Breakdowns are vehicles multiplied by the rate per hundred: Aylsham 8.8, Bickley 8.4, Chalfont 8.9, Draycott 8.5, Elstree 12.6, Fordham 5.7. Elstree is highest. The worst rate belongs to Draycott, which runs the fewest vehicles.

questions.prompt:
Rank the depots by revenue and separately by driver satisfaction, highest first in each. Which depot's two ranks differ most?

Depot | Vehicles | Breakdowns per 100 vehicles | Annual revenue | Driver satisfaction
Aylsham | 340 | 2.6 | GBP 512,000.00 | 63
Bickley | 205 | 4.1 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88
Chalfont | 470 | 1.9 | GBP 690,000.00 | 54
Draycott | 160 | 5.3 | GBP 246,000.00 | 84
Elstree | 395 | 3.2 | GBP 578,000.00 | 71
Fordham | 260 | 2.2 | GBP 402,000.00 | 79
options: A. Chalfont
B. Aylsham
C. Bickley
D. Draycott
E. Elstree
questions.explanation: By revenue: Chalfont, Elstree, Aylsham, Fordham, Bickley, Draycott. By satisfaction: Bickley, Draycott, Fordham, Elstree, Aylsham, Chalfont. Rank gaps: Aylsham 2, Bickley 4, Chalfont 5, Draycott 4, Elstree 2, Fordham 1. Chalfont differs by 5.
